title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week, the space industry is witnessing a mix of successes and setbacks, with Skyroot Aerospace making headlines for its first successful launch while NASA pulls the plug on a lunar lander mission. Meanwhile, budget allocations and new partnerships signal ongoing shifts in defense and space resilience strategies.

themes.title: Skyroot's Successful Launch
themes.body: Skyroot Aerospace has successfully reached orbit with its Vikram-1 rocket, marking a significant milestone for India's private space sector. This achievement adds pressure on other players to keep pace in an increasingly competitive market.

themes.title: NASA's Lunar Lander Setback
themes.body: NASA's decision to terminate the Draper lunar lander mission highlights the challenges of ambitious space exploration projects. As priorities shift, the agency's focus may turn to more viable alternatives.

themes.title: Defense Budget Boost
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup has allocated an additional $1.4 billion to enhance space resilience, reflecting a growing recognition of the strategic importance of space. This funding could pave the way for new technologies and collaborations in the defense sector.

themes.title: SpaceX's Ongoing Challenges
themes.body: SpaceX continues to grapple with operational hurdles, as evidenced by the aborted Starship Flight 13 launch attempt. Despite its dominance, the company must navigate logistical challenges to maintain its edge in the industry.
